extracted.intended_audience: researchers submitting or reviewing PCI Registered Reports (authors, reviewers, recommenders, managing board members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for submitting, reviewing, recommending, and publishing Registered Reports through the PCI Registered Reports community, covering Stage 1 and Stage 2 requirements, recommender/reviewer roles, equity measures, and related procedures (e.g., RRFP funding partnerships).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 submission content
rubrics_metrics.description: At Stage 1, authors submit their research question(s), theory and hypotheses (where applicable), detailed methods and analysis plans, and any preliminary data as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 1 submissions are peer reviewed in detail; the Stage 1 dossier should contain sufficient detail on question, theory, hypotheses, methods and analysis to allow evaluation prior to data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-principle acceptance (IPA) commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that are favourably assessed receive in-principle acceptance (IPA), which commits PCI RR to recommending the final article regardless of the outcomes, provided the authors adhere to their approved protocol and interpret the results in line with the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPA is conditional on adherence to the approved protocol and appropriate interpretation of results; following IPA, authors must register the approved protocol and later submit Stage 2 for assessment of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration after IPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Following IPA, authors then register their approved protocol in a recognised repository, either publicly or under a temporary embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration of the approved protocol is a required step after receiving IPA; repositories may allow temporary embargoes if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 manuscript content and permitted analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing the research, authors submit a Stage 2 manuscript that includes the approved protocol plus results and discussion, which may include clearly labelled post hoc analyses in addition to the preregistered outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post hoc analyses must be clearly labelled as such; the Stage 2 manuscript must present the approved protocol alongside outcomes and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 assessment criteria: protocol compliance & justified conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers from Stage 1 return to assess the completed Stage 2 manuscript, focusing on compliance with protocol and whether the conclusions are justified by the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation concentrates on whether authors adhered to the approved methods and whether their interpretations follow from the data; results per se do not affect the prior IPA if protocol was followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender role and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommender is very similar to a journal editor. They are responsible for finding at least two reviewers, collecting reviews, and making manuscript recommendations based on the reviews. The recommender signs all decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders may request one or several rounds of review and ultimately sign the decision letter; authors may suggest recommenders during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity and signing options
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may choose to remain anonymous or to sign their reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI RR supports anonymised or non-anonymised review tracks; reviewers' choice to sign or remain anonymous is respected and reviews (signed or anonymous) are published with the recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission tracks and embargo options
rubrics_metrics.description: Various submission tracks are available, including standard or scheduled review, and anonymised or non-anonymised review. Authors can also keep their Stage 1 manuscripts under private embargo until Stage 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors choose the submission track that fits their needs (timing and anonymity); private embargo option allows Stage 1 to remain inaccessible until Stage 2 if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender recommendation article requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recommender decides to recommend a report, they write a recommendation: essentially a short article, similar to a News & Views piece, describing the context of the study and explaining why this research is particularly interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendation accompanies the published reviews and editorial correspondence; it should contextualise the study and justify the recommendation for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and publication of reviews and correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommendation and all of the editorial correspondence (reviews, recommender's decisions, authors’ replies) associated with the recommended report are published by PCI RR and assigned a DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI RR publishes the complete set of Stage 1 and Stage 2 reviews solicited by PCI RR (signed or anonymous) and the recommender's decision letters; when a Stage 2 RR is published in a journal it should contain a link to these reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to publish in PCI RR-friendly journals without further peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of RRs that are positively recommended have the option to publish their articles in the growing list of PCI RR-friendly journals that have committed to accepting PCI RR recommendations without further peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may choose to take up this option; PCI RR maintains lists of friendly and interested journals and updates on journal participation are provided (including warnings when journals withdraw).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusiveness and equity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI is attentive to equity and inclusion at all steps: bringing underrepresented people among authors, reviewers, recommenders, and Managing Board members; specific recommendations are made to reviewers, recommenders, and Managing Board members to increase equity and inclusiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools include possibility to submit articles anonymously, transparency in evaluation, Managing Board consideration of underrepresentation when appointing recommenders, template messages with equity recommendations, possibility to review anonymously, and signatory status of C4DISC.

rubrics_metrics.name: RRFP (Registered Reports Funding Partnerships) concurrent review model
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the RRFP model, the funder and PCI RR will review a Stage 1 RR (or set of RRs) concurrently (or near concurrently), and if both PCI RR and the funder judge the proposal to be of sufficient quality then the funder will award funding at the same time as PCI RR awards in principle acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RRFPs compress grant review and Stage 1 RR review into a single process and can be integrated with ethics and regulatory review; intended for researchers without prior grant funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and recommender training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI RR provides workshops, slide-based tutorials, and an editor/recommender test that recommenders must pass before being assigned their first RR; these resources are CC-BY 4.0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources include a 1-hour interactive workshop, a public editor test to learn the process, and a short tutorial explaining Stage 1 recommendation components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural transparency about manuscript hosting and DOI policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript itself remains on the preprint server and is not separately published by PCI RR; PCI RR publishes reviews/recommendations and assigns a DOI to the set of reviews and recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain the preprint as the primary manuscript location; PCI RR's publication of reviews and recommendation (with DOI) creates a citable record of the peer review and recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship, copyright and licensing of PCI RR-published texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of comments, reviews and recommendations retain copyright under CC-BY for texts published after and including 24/01/2022 and under CC-BY-ND before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI RR provides guidance on how to cite articles and clarifies copyright/licenses for different publication dates.
